sasha: heads-up — running a long-seq workload on the paged-flash fp8 kernel and got hard infs from softmax, sequence=4096, batch=4. attaching a tiny log snippet and stack. :eyes:

sasha: ```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] runtime: cuda kernel paged_flash_fp8_forward launch
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] WARN softmax: max_logit=102.3 min_logit=-1.2 -> exp overflow -> INF detected
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] ERROR output contains NaN/INF
```

sasha: repro command I used: `./bench --model gorilla-8b --kernel paged-flash-fp8 --seq 4096 --batch 4 --profile`

david: can repro locally when I run with the same flags. quick observation: the fp8 quant scale for some heads is ~1e-2 which pushes logits high after q*dequant accumulation.

maria: on bf16/fp16 we don't hit this, so it's definitely quantization + softmax instability. suspect missing log-sum-exp or clamping in the fused kernel path.

jonathan: profiling numbers from my run: paged-flash fp8 gives +18% throughput vs fused-bf16 for cold KV, but p99 latency spikes when it falls back (we see ~30% latency tail due to per-request kernel switch). also noticed heavy memcpy during KV page-ins when seq > 2048.

ci-bench-bot: posted perf artifacts -> https://ci.company.internal/bench/1712554321 (bench summary attached) :white_check_mark:

sasha: proposed mitigation: 1) add a numeric guard in kernel selector: if estimated max_logit > 80 or (max_logit - min_logit) > 60 then force stable-bf16-softmax kernel. 2) add a per-head scaling sanity check when dequantizing (clamp scales to min 1e-4). 3) reduce default batching heuristic for seq>2048 (e.g., max_batch = max(1, floor(8192 / seq))).

david: +1 to selector guard. small tweak: compute a cheap fast-path approximate max_logit from qkv accumulator stats on host before dispatch. that avoids launching the fp8 kernel only to fall back.

maria: for the kernel change itself we should implement log-sum-exp in the fused kernel: do `m = max(logits); sum = sum(exp(logits - m)); softmax = exp(logits - m) / sum`. but be mindful of extra fp32 ops cost on the fp8 path. maybe only enable LSE when dynamic range exceeds threshold.

jonathan: agreed. adding hysteresis to avoid oscillation: once we switch to stable kernel for a request, keep stable kernel for next N requests if avg seq doesn't drop below threshold. prevents flip-flop under bursty traffic.

sasha: quick patch plan:
- runtime: kernel_selector change + host-side quick max_logit estimate (PR: sasha/guard-softmax-171)
- runtime: batching heuristic adjustment (PR: sasha/batch-cap-171)
- kernel: fused paged-flash fp8 add optional LSE path gated by a flag (PR: maria/paged-lse-171)
- infra: add randomized numeric regression tests to CI that fuzz logits including extreme patterns and verify no inf/nan and closeness to bf16 baseline (PR: david/fuzz-softmax-171)

maria: I'll own the kernel LSE flag and implement minimal fp32 accumulation with a compile-time fastpath. estimate perf hit ~5-8% when enabled.

david: I'll add the host estimator and the CI fuzz harness. suggest we also log when selector forced stable kernel so we can quantify how often this fires in prod.

ci-bench-bot: benchmark job queued: job id 1712554321-try1, will post results when done.

sasha: one more note — KV cache behavior: when page-in rate is high (many long contexts), memory copy jitter causes batching heuristics to mis-estimate token concurrency. let's add a page-in overhead estimate into the batch cost model (simple: cost += pages * page_cost_ms).

jonathan: good call. we should also consider preferring kernels that stream KV without allocating giant temporaries for page-in heavy workloads.

maria: let's aim for a canary on dedicated stg cluster: enable fp8 paged-flash with LSE flag off for X% traffic and turn on selector guard. monitor NaN/infs and latency tail.

sasha: plan accepted. I'm opening the two runtime PRs now. tagging @david @maria for reviews. :thumbsup:

david: ack, will review tonight.

maria: ack, will start kernel patch tomorrow.

sasha: thanks all — keeping this thread open for rollout notes.
